model_annotation: Figure 15 presents three separate pie charts illustrating the distribution of quantifiers and operations across three distinct reasoning domains: Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive. The first pie chart, labeled “Categorical,” is divided into four segments: “Existential Quantifiers” (15.12%, light green), “Negation” (27.91%, orange), “Universal Quantifiers” (29.07%, light blue), and “Limiter” (27.91%, light pink). The second chart, “Approximate Number Generation,” contains three segments: “Absolute Absence” (18.71%, light purple), “Comparative Relationships” (36.26%, medium blue), and “Approximate Quantifiers” (45.03%, beige). The third chart, “Disjunctive & Conjunctive,” is split into two nearly equal parts: “Disjunctive” (49.51%, light blue) and “Conjunctive” (50.49%, light purple). Each chart includes percentage labels within the slices and uses distinct colors to differentiate categories, with no legend provided on the page. The segments within each pie chart appear to be arranged in descending order of proportion, starting from the top-right and moving clockwise.
